synthesis: The GL Kits admin page (/app/gl-kits, the prior GL Kits page) renders one row per Kit (a login identity for a person) instead of one row per physical GL camera. The fix re-keys the table to GL identity from the ClickHouse-only, MV-fed zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name, scoped by a PostgreSQL-derived kit_id list, rolling the two existing per-kit ClickHouse lookups (last scan, 14-day GPS reporting) up to the GL with max()/any() semantics; adds sortability to both computed columns; defaults to 100 rows/page. Because Eloquent cannot sort a getStateUsing column, row identity must move off getEloquentQuery() onto Filament's ->records() array-record API (in-repo precedent: app/Filament/Widgets/Client/ClientTable.php:138). Two consequences the ticket does not address, both surfaced by measurement: (1) the largest single group is NOT org 1143's 49 GLs but org_id=1 (InsightLPR) at 524 GLs from 239 kits, over 10x larger; and (2) moving row IDENTITY onto a ClickHouse read changes production failure behavior — today a ClickHouse outage still renders every row with 'Unknown' columns because rows come from PostgreSQL, whereas under the ticket's design a GL-discovery failure yields NO rows at all. That is a resilience regression on a HOTFIX, and the AC 'a GL whose ClickHouse lookup failed renders Unknown' presupposes a row exists to carry it.

questions.q: When the ClickHouse read that discovers GL identity (zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name) fails, what should the page show? Today a ClickHouse outage still renders every row with 'Unknown' columns, because rows come from PostgreSQL. Under this design a discovery failure means no rows at all, which looks identical to an org that genuinely owns no GLs.
questions.answer: Accept the empty table. Ship exactly as the ticket specifies: a GL-discovery failure renders zero rows. reportClickhouseFailure() still logs and calls report(), so the outage reaches error tracking even though the admin sees an empty table. ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF, recorded deliberately: this is a resilience regression versus today, where rows come from PostgreSQL and survive a ClickHouse outage with 'Unknown' columns. Must be stated in the PR body and the Build Record, not buried.

questions.q: How should the 5 ClickHouse-free tests in GlKitsResourceAccessTest be preserved? They assert specific-row presence, which now needs a ClickHouse-only table with no pgsql-bridge equivalent (measured: no zod or clarity schema exists in the local test Postgres at all). Their docblock says the split exists so deleting canAccess() or the org scope cannot produce a green run.
questions.answer: Split by what needs ClickHouse. GlKitsResourceAccessTest stays ClickHouse-free and asserts tenancy/authorization on the PostgreSQL kit query that feeds ClickHouse (org scope, kit_type=1, excludingDeleted) plus the non-admin 403 — so deleting canAccess() or the org_id scope still fails a test with ClickHouse down. The row-RENDERING assertions move into GlKitsResourceTest, which runs against real ClickHouse in CI. No new machinery and no migration. Re-asked and re-confirmed after the driver established there is NO test-time PostgreSQL bridge to extend: zod.kit_last_scan has no PostgreSQL migration, local-clickhouse-schema.sql defines only a clarity schema and is applied by hand rather than by the suite, and CI sets CLICKHOUSE_DRIVER=clickhouse. The rejected alternative would have required a real Laravel migration creating a ClickHouse shim table in production PostgreSQL, hand-applied, on a hotfix.

questions.q: Sort rank order for the tri-state Reporting badge (Reporting / Not Reporting / Unknown). No existing precedent in this codebase orders a tri-state badge.
questions.answer: Best-known first, and mixed renders Not Reporting. Ascending sort ranks Reporting, then Not Reporting, then Unknown. A GL whose kits are a mix of Not Reporting and Unknown with none Reporting renders 'Not Reporting', because at least one of its kits was actually checked and came back negative.

questions.q: When a GL's kits are a mix of 'Not Reporting' and 'Unknown' with none Reporting, does the GL render Not Reporting or Unknown?
questions.answer: Not Reporting. At least one of the GL's kits was actually checked and came back negative, so the page can honestly say 'Not Reporting'. Unknown is reserved for the cases where NOTHING was checked — the read failed, or no kit mapped to the GL has a scanner mapping at all.

questions.q: Should the GL column stay searchable? 'name' is searchable() today; with ->records() the closure owns search via the search/columnSearches injection, so it is opt-in work rather than free.

questions.q: Do kit_type=1 kits that have never scanned disappear from the page entirely?
questions.answer: Yes, and it is inherent to the specified data source, not an implementation gap: GL identity only exists once a scan has recorded that camera_name (the MV is fed from public_scans). Today such a kit shows a Never / Not Reporting placeholder row. This is a real behavior change and belongs in the PR description.

questions.q: Should the production query use the ticket's literal join against zod.public_kits for org scoping?
questions.answer: No. zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name has no org_id (measured: 2 columns only), and OrgKitLastScanQuery's docblock documents why kit ids must come from PostgreSQL rather than a ClickHouse org_id. The ticket's join was a one-off investigation query, not a production scoping mechanism. Scope from the PG-derived kit_id list; this is strictly safer and keeps tenancy in one place.

notes: PRIMARY RISK: this ticket moves row IDENTITY from PostgreSQL to ClickHouse. Every other Filament resource here keeps identity in PostgreSQL and degrades only computed COLUMNS on a CH failure. This is the first case where the row SET can vanish during an outage — a resilience regression relative to the current buggy-but-resilient page, shipped as a HOTFIX. Q1 exists to decide it deliberately rather than by omission.

ACCEPTED RISK (Q1, Dalton 2026-09-04): a ClickHouse GL-discovery failure renders an empty table, indistinguishable to the admin from an org that owns no GLs. Today's page survives an outage because rows come from PostgreSQL. The decision was made with that trade-off stated. reportClickhouseFailure() keeps the outage visible in error tracking. This MUST appear in the PR body and Build Record.

zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name is exactly 2 columns (kit_id Int32, camera_name String) — no org_id, no _peerdb_* columns. MV-fed (REFRESH EVERY 5 MINUTE, incremental from zod.public_scans), not a CDC mirror. Applying a CDC soft-delete predicate to it errors, as the ticket warns.

FINAL and SELECT DISTINCT collapse the table identically (raw 12,414 -> 10,600 both ways). The ticket's cited 10,598 is the deduped figure; the ~2-row drift is 3 days of MV growth, not a contradiction. FINAL matches this repo's stated ReplacingMergeTree convention.

Largest single group is org_id=1 (InsightLPR) at 524 distinct GLs from 239 kit_type=1 kits — 10x the ticket's 49-GL anchor. Real all-time data (zod.public_kits FINAL and no-FINAL agree at 239, so not a stale-CDC artifact); the MV never expires rows, so treat 524 as a floor.
zod.public_kits IS well-merged and ORDER BY id, so it does not carry zod.kit_last_scan's stale-org-row risk — moot under the recommended design, which never queries it for scoping.
Array-record identity: build the underlying collection keyed by GL (->keyBy()) so Filament's mapWithKeys defaults __key to the GL string and tests can address rows by that string.

ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows Throwable in production|testing, so a failed read looks EMPTY rather than thrown. That is exactly why GlKitsResource catches locally to produce 'Unknown'. A new query class must preserve that distinction or the Unknown state dies silently.

.claude/commands/chlocal.md reads from a SIBLING path (../chlocal/...) which does not resolve from this nested worktree; ~/Herd/chlocal is a real sibling of the main checkout. Use an absolute path or run the procedure from the main checkout.

Local full-suite runs need php -d memory_limit=2G vendor/bin/phpunit (or PHPRC): php artisan test OOMs during DISCOVERY at 128M and still exits 0, a false green (the OOM-during-discovery test runner issue). Expect ~8 pre-existing failures.
RequiresClickhouse TRUNCATEs hardcoded clarity.* / zod.* literals, so local CH databases must be named literally clarity and zod, and teardown must never drop them.
Comments and docblocks in this repo stay minimal (user preference). The existing GlKitsResource docblocks are load-bearing 'why' notes — adapt them, do not multiply them.

resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Per request, single org: PG kit_id list <=272 ints -> one CH IN-list query returning <=524 (kit_id, camera_name) pairs -> PHP inversion to a <=524-key GL map -> two further CH IN-list lookups bounded by the same <=272 kit_ids -> rollup, sort, slice in PHP. All structures are hundreds of small scalars and short strings — kilobytes, not megabytes — even at the measured worst case. No array_chunk, no accumulator spanning multiple orgs; the once() memos are per-request and per-$orgId. The risk class here is query SHAPE (an unbounded IN-list if an org ever grows enormously), not allocation x concurrency. Concurrency is bounded by simultaneous admins of one large org, which is small. Contrast the rejected clarity.scans_hot alternative at 4.2 s / 412 MB per org page load.
